title: The recovery that drained the card
subtitle: Four failed engine loads took a shared GPU from 1,801 MiB free to 2, because partial allocations were never released; the fix made creation crash-safe and made the admission arithmetic match the allocation it predicts

stats.label: failed engine loads in a row, each one passing admission
the CUDA context the admission arithmetic had left out
MiB, the engine's whole allowance beside a 30B serving model

lede: The tool-discovery engine lives on a GPU beside a 30-billion-parameter serving model, in a fixed allowance and no more. An admission check compares the engine's requirement with the card's free memory before anything is allocated, and refuses with the shortfall if it does not fit. That check once passed every time while the engine failed to load every time, and the card drained. Engine creation allocated its buffers in sequence, and when a later allocation failed, the earlier ones were not freed before the error returned. Each retry therefore started with less free memory than the last, passed admission because the arithmetic looked only at the engine's own total, and failed further along.
quote: A failed load leaves the card as it found it.
evidence: GPU memory management: engine creation made crash-safe after four failed loads took a shared GPU from 1,801 MiB free to 2.
Admission control for GPU memory: admission arithmetic made to mirror the allocator, including the ~503 MiB CUDA context it had left out.
Incident root-cause analysis: four failed loads, each passing admission, traced to partial allocations never released and a context missing from the arithmetic.
Inference serving on shared GPUs: an engine held to a 2,740 MiB allowance beside a 30B serving model, with cache pages reserved per request before admission.
author: Corey James
